unit.why: A short first-person memorate by R. Nahman of Horodenka about his cold and hot mikveh immersions, which failed to free him from alien thoughts until he turned to the Besht's wisdom.

stories.summary_en: R. Nahman of Horodenka recounts that as a great hasid he immersed daily in an unbearably cold mikveh and in a scalding one without feeling the heat, yet could not rid himself of alien thoughts until he had recourse to the Besht's wisdom.

tags.why: Daily ritual immersion is the core practice described.

quotes: ומצאתי המקוה חם מאוד עד שכמעט בערו הכתלים
tags.why: The action takes place in the mikveh.

quotes: לא הייתי יכול לפטור מן מחשבות זרות
tags.why: The story is about his struggle with alien thoughts.

quotes: שבדור זה לא יוכל לסבול שום אדם מקוה כזו
tags.why: Extreme cold and hot immersions are a form of bodily mortification.

quotes: ואעפ״כ לא הייתי יכול לפטור מן מחשבות זרות
tags.why: The ascetic remedy fails to work.
The Besht's wisdom succeeds where the ascetic means failed.
The text is framed as a tale heard from a named hasid.
He was insensible to a scalding heat for an hour, a quasi-miraculous feat.

missing_concepts: contrast between ascetic piety and Beshtian method
